chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) pluck his two cheeks and line his beard.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) do with his beard and cheeks?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Kafi highlights the physical grooming of Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), specifically his practice of plucking stray hairs from the cheeks ('aridayn) and arranging his beard. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary textual basis for the recommended etiquette (adab) of maintaining a neat and dignified appearance, distinguishing the beard from the moustache. The act reflects the broader Islamic principle of fitrah (natural disposition), emphasizing cleanliness and self-respect as acts of worship.
